meta.name: Capture Gmail website leads in Google Sheets with internal email alerts

parameters.content:
## Real estate lead qualification mini CRM

### How it works

1. The workflow watches Gmail for new real estate inquiry emails.
2. It extracts contact details and classifies the lead as Buyer, Seller, Rental, or General Inquiry.
3. It scores the lead using intent signals such as valuation, viewing, budget, urgency, and phone availability.
4. It checks Google Sheets for an existing lead with the same email address.
5. New leads are saved to a CRM-style sheet and activity log, then routed into Hot, Warm, or Cold follow-up paths.
6. The workflow sends internal alerts and a personalized auto-reply for new valid leads.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Connect Gmail credentials in all Gmail nodes.
- [ ] Connect Google Sheets credentials in all Google Sheets nodes.
- [ ] Create a Google Sheet with tabs named `Leads` and `Activity Log`.
- [ ] Add the required columns listed in the sheet setup notes.
- [ ] Replace the placeholder Google Sheet ID in the Google Sheets nodes.
- [ ] Replace the internal alert email addresses.
- [ ] Adjust the Gmail search query to match your lead source.

### Customization

Update the keyword lists and scoring thresholds in `Extract Classify And Score Lead` to match your market, lead forms, and sales process.

## Capture real estate inquiries

The Gmail trigger looks for recent inquiry emails related to buying, selling, renting, valuations, viewings, and property questions.

Customize the Gmail search query if your website form uses different subject lines.

## Extract and score lead details

The Code node cleans the email body and extracts the fields a real estate team needs:

- Name
- Email address
- Phone number
- Lead type
- Property type
- Location
- Budget
- Timeframe

It then calculates a lead score and priority from urgency and intent keywords.

## Handle missing contact details

If no email address is found, the workflow sends an internal manual-review alert instead of trying to add an incomplete CRM record.

This prevents bad data from entering the lead sheet.

## Check for duplicate leads

The workflow searches the `Leads` sheet by email address before creating a new row.

If the email already exists, it sends a duplicate alert so the sales team can review the existing record instead of creating noise in the CRM.

## Save CRM and activity records

New leads are written to the `Leads` tab with classification, score, priority, and follow-up due date.

The workflow also writes a separate activity record to the `Activity Log` tab. This gives the team a simple history of captured lead events instead of only a raw list of contacts.

## Send a personalized auto-reply

For new valid leads, Gmail sends a basic confirmation email back to the contact.

Customize the message so it matches the agency brand and asks for the details your team needs before a call.

## Route leads by priority

The Switch node separates Hot, Warm, and Cold leads.

Hot leads trigger urgent alerts for immediate response. Warm leads get standard follow-up reminders. Cold leads are still logged, but they are handled with a lower-priority summary.

## Leads sheet columns

Create a `Leads` tab with these columns:

Created At | Name | Email | Phone | Lead Type | Property Type | Location | Budget | Timeframe | Lead Score | Lead Priority | Matched Keywords | Follow Up Due | Subject | Message | Source | Duplicate

The duplicate lookup depends on the `Email` column.

## Activity log columns

Create an `Activity Log` tab with these columns:

Logged At | Email | Lead Priority | Event | Recommended Action | Next Follow Up | Notes

Use this tab to review what happened after each captured lead.

filters.q: newer_than:1d (subject:(property) OR subject:(real estate) OR subject:(buy) OR subject:(sell) OR subject:(rent) OR subject:(valuation) OR subject:(viewing) OR subject:(inquiry))
